summary.text: Kyle Koehler is serving his first term in the Ohio Senate for District 10, which encompasses Clark, Greene, and Clinton counties. He chairs the Senate Workforce Development Committee.

paragraphs.text: A life-long resident of Clark County, Koehler graduated from Springfield Catholic Central in 1980 and from Wright State University in 1984 with a Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science.

He spent seven years working for government contractors at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and for the Navy as a Senior Software Engineer, then returned in 1990 to his family business, K.K. Tool, as a Vice President in charge of Design and Development.
Koehler served in the Ohio House from 2015 to 2022 and chaired the Agriculture and Rural Development Committee for four years.
His House work included the reform of payday lending (HB 123 of the 132nd General Assembly) and of occupational licensing (HB 263 of the 133rd).
In the 136th General Assembly he is also Vice Chair of the Agriculture & Natural Resources Committee and the Sunset Review Committee.
Koehler and his wife, Kathrin, have been married for 37 years and have five adult children.
